scenario: tmpfs mounted at /dev/shm with the bare usrquota flag in its super options (user quota accounting and enforcement enabled on that mount) — the contract's tmpfs row must classify it enabled/enforced with basis tmpfs_quota_option.

fixture.mountinfo:
29 29 0:24 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - ext4 /dev/nvme0n1p3 rw,errors=remount-ro
65 29 0:30 /@home /home rw,relatime shared:2 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=257,subvol=/@home
244 29 259:1 / /tmp rw,relatime - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p1 rw,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=256k,noquota
30 29 0:26 / /dev/shm rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:9 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,size=402653184k,usrquota

rationale: Contract §C2 quota-classification table, tmpfs row 1: 'tmpfs | any of quota,usrquota,grpquota or a key ending _hardlimit | enabled | enforced | tmpfs_quota_option'. Mount resolution (contract §C2 'Mount resolution', parsed per proc.rst §3.5): the fixture's four mountinfo lines give candidate mounts for realpath '/dev/shm' — the ext4 line at mount point '/' and the tmpfs line at mount point '/dev/shm' — and the longest mount point wins, so the tmpfs line is chosen; its filesystem type (field m+2) is 'tmpfs' and its super options (field m+4, the last mountinfo field) are 'rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,size=402653184k,usrquota'. Comma-splitting that string and taking the text before '=' per key yields the quota-related key 'usrquota' (a bare flag, no '='), which is a member of {quota,usrquota,grpquota}; therefore quota_state=enabled, enforcement=enforced, basis=tmpfs_quota_option (the tmpfs row's second clause, 'none of them', does not apply because 'usrquota' is present). Device check: tmpfs is not btrfs, so the chosen mount's major:minor (field 3 of the tmpfs line, '0:26') must equal the path's st_dev; the fixture's st_dev '0:26' matches, so the device check does not degrade the row to 'unknown'/device_mismatch (device_check is not among the compared fields, but the fixture keeps it consistent). Verdict precedence (contract §C2 'Verdict precedence'): a path with quota_state=enabled yields exit 1 and finding_id QUOTA_ENABLED, which is a runway-reporting finding and not a failure claim. Source anchors: S084 = Documentation/filesystems/tmpfs.rst at v7.2, quota mount-option table 129-143, in particular the usrquota row at 135-136 ('User quota accounting and enforcement is enabled on the mount.') and the mount-time-only note at 145 ('None of the quota related mount options can be set or changed on remount.') — this supports both 'enabled' and 'enforced' for the usrquota flag; S082 = Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst §3.5 at v7.2, lines 1965-1990, field table 1970-1983 (major:minor = field 3 at 1975, separator at 1980, filesystem type at 1981, mount source at 1982, super options at 1983), which fixes the field positions used to read the filesystem type and the super options. Out-of-band realism check (NOT among S077-S084, unregistered, used only to confirm that the fixture's option string is kernel-shaped and not to derive the expectation): upstream v7.2 mm/shmem.c has fsparam_flag("usrquota", Opt_usrquota) at 4462, case Opt_usrquota at 4626-4631 setting ctx->quota_types |= QTYPE_MASK_USR, and the superblock show_options emitting seq_printf(seq, ",usrquota") at 4878-4879 when sb_has_quota_active(root->d_sb, USRQUOTA) — i.e. the kernel prints the bare key 'usrquota' into the mountinfo super-options column, which is exactly where the contract instructs the probe to read quota keys.
